title: D2's project tiers are written out by hand at four sites beside project_owns_command, and nothing keeps them in step
body:
FOUND by cc's critic-shell review of issue 0113's build on 2026-09-23.

0113 added `project_owns_command` in lib/resolve. It is true when the project has a handler of its own (a file, or a mapped `handler:`) or a command-level `run:`. Doctor's shadow report and help's choice of page both ask it. The same tiers of D2's order are still written out by hand, in the same order, at four more sites:
- command_active (lib/resolve:312 and :327): a project handler or a `run:` makes the command active.
- _command_runnable (lib/cmd/doctor:324-325): the first two of the five sources run_command consults.
- command_origin (lib/help:267-279): the three tiers, each with its own label.
- print_topic (lib/help:630): asks project_owns_command a second time. help_file returns 1 both when the project owns the command and when neither root has a page, so print_topic has to work out which one happened.

Each site is exercised and they agree today. Nothing keeps them in step, though, so a new tier, or a stricter has_project_handler, would change some sites and not others. The review's scenario: has_project_handler starts requiring the mapped target to exist, and a project sets `upgrade.handler: gone`. help then prints devbin's page and trailer, while the trailer's own `from:` line says "project handler gone (mapped)". That is two answers to one question on one screen.

SEQUENCED AFTER 0117 (vc, 2026-09-23). 0117 changes builtin_has_default_run and touches command_origin and _command_runnable, two of the sites above, so this refactor lands on top of it and keeps 0117's arms green.

NOT DONE IN 0113: command_active is on the dispatch path of every command, so the change is a piece of work in its own right with its own review. It also answers a different question at each site: whether the command exists, whether typing it would do anything, which tier to name, and whether devbin's page may speak for it. What the sites share is the project tiers.

FIX: one helper that names the tier (handler, mapped, run, or none). command_origin uses the name for its label and every other site uses the yes or no. help_file says why it returned nothing, so print_topic decides once.

FOUR SMALLER POINTS, three from the same review and in the same code, and one from 0113's test-check critic:
- print_topic ignores cat's status (`cat ...; return 0`, with 0113's trailer between the two). If a caller reaches it from an `if`, `&&` or `||` context, errexit is off, so an unreadable page prints nothing, then the full trailer, and exits 0. On the bin/devbin path errexit is on, and the review drove it: exit 1, cat's error on stderr, nothing on stdout. Fix: `cat -- "${file#*$'\t'}" || return`.
- The comment on the no-page stub says "A command the project owns or declared is the project's". "Declared" means a command devbin does not ship, and the condition is right. The word misleads, though: a built-in the project extends with an option of its own still gets devbin's no-page stub, which is correct, since that page is devbin's to write (0115). The comment should say "a command devbin does not ship".
- help_file's `${DEVBIN_DIR:-}` and `${DEVBIN_LIB:-}` are half-guards. Unset, they read `/help` and `/pages` at the filesystem root, while lib/resolve reads DEVBIN_DIR bare under nounset. bin/devbin always sets and exports both, so neither case is reachable.
- The unavailable reasons name the config by its absolute path: `it is disabled in /private/var/.../bin/.devbin/config.yaml`, and the same for the language sentence. All three sites spell it `${DEVBIN_DIR:-bin/.devbin}/config.yaml` (lib/resolve:157, :184 and :220), and bin/devbin sets DEVBIN_DIR absolute, so the fallback, the one relative spelling, never prints. `help --why` has always shown it that way. Since 0113 the same text follows every shipped page, where `bin/.devbin/config.yaml`, relative to the project root, says the same in a fraction of the width. help.bats matches these rows with `.+` after "in ", so a relative path does not move an arm.

AND ONE LIMIT OF THE RULE ITSELF, which binds whoever ships the first option sub-page. Ownership is decided per command, never per option. A shipped `lib/pages/<cmd>.d/<opt>.md` would answer `help <cmd> <opt>` in a project that overrides that option with `commands.<cmd>.options.<opt>.run`, so the page would describe code that does not run there, and only the trailer's `from:` line would say so. No sub-page ships today; help.bats plants one only to test the order of the two roots.

AND DOCTOR'S NOTE, added at vc's request on 2026-09-23. doctor's note for a name offered with nothing to run (lib/cmd/doctor:312-313) prints one generic remedy for every name it lists: "each needs commands.<name>.run, or a handler in bin/.devbin/cmd/". Since 0117, that list can also hold a built-in whose devbin handler is missing from the install, and for that case the generic remedy is the wrong advice. unrunnable_why already says the right thing for each case, and the refusal prints it. So the refactor gives each listed name unrunnable_why's own sentence, making doctor, the refusal and `help --why` one answer at a fourth site. The shipped pages must then not quote the note's remedy, and 0115's are written that way.

AND TWO LIVE SITES, found by 0115's page audit on 2026-09-23 and driven by cc at 4c9d5a7. They break this issue's premise that each site is exercised and they agree today, so its severity rises from low to medium. Both are sites of the one helper this issue asks for.
- bin/devbin's `all` branch (bin/devbin:641-654) asks has_project_handler, not project_owns_command. A command-level `run:` owns every other argument list of its command, but not `all`. DRIVEN with `commands.clean.run: scripts/myclean`: `bin/devbin clean rust --dry-run` ran "scripts/myclean rust --dry-run", while `bin/devbin clean all --dry-run` ran devbin's own rust arm, scan and seal included. `help clean` meanwhile said "Resolves from: config commands.clean.run". A project that replaced clean to control what it removes gets devbin's removal from `all`.
- --iex is offered where devbin's server does not run. _framework_option and framework_option_takes (lib/resolve:1160, :1182) ask whether a reader of the flag is ACTIVE, never whether devbin's implementation is what runs. DRIVEN with `commands.server.run: mix myserver`: `bin/devbin server --iex` ran "mix myserver" unchanged, exit 0, and help still listed --iex as "Start the server in IEx rather than plain". A project handler may read DEVBIN_OPT_IEX, so the helper's answer is an input here rather than the whole rule, and the fix says what --iex means over a command the project owns.

## Resolution

Fixed at eb97d33. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. lib/resolve states each order of D2 once, and the code that runs acts on it: arg_route is the dispatcher's route, option_run_tier is run_option's order, command_tier is run_command's, project_tier names the project's tier, and option_leaf follows a route to what runs at its end, which help's option_origin and check's fmt arms read. route_word_at is the one reading of the route word, asked by arg_route and by bin/devbin. A command-level run: owns its command as a handler does: option_active, builtin_options and option_unavailable_reason displace the built-in option set under project_owns_command, and a declared option with no run: of its own goes to the command's line. `all` sweeps where there are options, goes on to a handler or an option-less built-in that answers for itself, and is refused, exit 1 with a pointer to the bare command, over a run: line with no option to run (hv's option (b), 2026-09-24), which closes the `test all` false green over `cargo test`. The same holds past devbin's gate flags (`test --purge all`, `rq --purge one`), on hv's ruling, with the flag list stated once in is_gate_flag. --iex no longer counts over a run: line unless options.iex.commands names it. help's --why labels command_tier and option_leaf, print_topic returns on cat's failure, doctor's _command_runnable asks command_tier with a remedy per name, and check format decides an owned fmt from option_leaf. fixture_run and fixture_ask are the arms' one helper. MEASURED across the 17 estates on 2026-09-24: four commands are owned by a run: line, none declares options, and no estate's behaviour changes; no estate owns fmt, and none owns server by a run:.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. Ownership is decided per command, never per option, so a shipped option sub-page would describe devbin's option in a project that overrides that one option; none ships, and help_file's comment says who decides first. A run: declared empty is refused `all` with a pointer to the bare command, which then refuses the empty line itself (0082), exit 1 both ways. fullcycle's and dormancy's reading of option_leaf are 0134's and 0135's.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell at each revision: v1's code pass raised 13 items, all taken in v2, and its test-check pass the false-green critical that hv's option (b) answers; v3's code pass 0 critical, 0 warnings, 4 recommendations, and its test-check pass 0 critical, 2 warnings, 3 recommendations, 5 style, all taken; v3c's delta 0 critical, 3 warnings, 3 recommendations, 1 style, all taken; v3d's delta one critical, two loops choosing the route word, answered by route_word_at, and its re-review 0 critical, 0 warnings, 1 recommendation, taken. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-25, approved at v3d on the patch, the interdiffs, both of hv's rulings built as ruled, and the evidence below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Over v2's code exactly the arms for option (b) were red, each for its reason; over the base every 0128 arm was red for its stated reason but a pin and two stated controls, and the funnel's 29 rows disagreed on exactly the 5 that 0128 changes; the gate-flag arm red over v3b's code, and its option rows over v3c's. 77 mutants, each against the arms it aims at: 76 killed. MP survives and is equivalent over the shipped catalogue: it swaps two rungs that differ only for a command with both lib/cmd/<cmd> and a catalogue default run, and none of the 21 shipped handlers has one.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the nine 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on b10dd41 (0139, 0128, 0133, 0130, 0142, 0143, 0144, 0146, 0147), on a clean checkout (head 308cf21), 2026-09-25 11:34:20Z to 12:09:20Z: 1907 of 1907 ok, 0 not ok, no gaps, its 5 skips the suite's declared ones. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree outside intent/.
